issues.description: The patch_classification section declares 'platform_only: True' and 'guard: "#ifdef __OHOS__"' for patch 0001-src-netinfo.c.patch, but the actual patch file does not contain any '#ifdef __OHOS__' guard. The patch is an unconditional replacement of (caddr_t) with (char *) that applies to all platforms. The metadata is inconsistent with the actual patch content and could be misleading to reviewers.
issues.fix_suggestion: Either: (1) Update the patch_classification metadata to reflect the actual unconditional nature of the patch (set platform_only to False and remove the guard field), or (2) If platform-only application is truly desired, add an '#ifdef __OHOS__' guard to the patch itself. Option (1) is preferred since (char *) is a valid replacement on all platforms and the unconditional patch is correct.

issues.description: The build() method directly modifies the generated 'configure' script via string replacement (content.replace('umask 077', 'umask 022')). Rule R6 states that modifications to generated files (configure, config.h, Makefile.in, etc.) should be handled through generate() or patches/. While the current approach is pragmatic — the configure script does not exist until autoreconf runs in build(), so generate() cannot modify it — the direct file manipulation in build() is technically outside the preferred workflow.
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider creating a patch file for the autotools input (e.g., configure.ac) if the umask setting originates from there, or document this as a known limitation with a clear comment explaining why the modification must happen in build() after autoreconf. The current approach is functional and pragmatic; this is a suggestion for better alignment with R6.

issues.description: The manifest.yaml uses the field name 'software:' instead of 'name:' as specified in code style rule 14 (which shows 'name: zlib'). Similarly, it uses 'build:' nested with 'system:' instead of the flat 'build_system:' field. The manifest comments reference 'ARCHIVE-SPEC v2.0' which may define a different schema. If the project has standardized on ARCHIVE-SPEC v2.0, this is acceptable; otherwise it deviates from the code style standard.
issues.fix_suggestion: Verify which specification the project follows for manifest.yaml. If ARCHIVE-SPEC v2.0 is the authoritative standard, no change needed. If code style rule 14 is the standard, align field names to use 'name:' and 'build_system:' for consistency.

issues.description: The test_package only runs 'macchanger --version' as a smoke test. While this is a valid binary execution test (passes R34 — it actually invokes the binary), it does not test the platform-specific functionality that the patch addresses (ioctl with SIOCETHTOOL and network interface MAC address operations). For a network interface tool classified under R40 '系统底层' category, the test coverage is minimal. However, this is understandable for CI since actual MAC address manipulation requires root privileges and physical network interfaces.
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider adding a test that at least invokes 'macchanger --list' or 'macchanger -s' (show current MAC) which would exercise more of the patched code path (network interface enumeration) without requiring root. If that's not feasible in CI, document the limitation in notes.md or test_package/MANIFEST.yml.
